audit.name: Security audit
audit.instructions: Audit the requested scope for concrete security risks. For each finding identify severity, file/symbol, exploit conditions, affected trust boundary and a precise remediation with an acceptance check. Clearly distinguish confirmed findings from unverified risks.

route.when: The user asks whether code is secure, or wants vulnerabilities, risky dependencies, exposed secrets or unsafe configuration reviewed.

route.when: The user wants work that was already done, their own changes or the previous result, checked or reviewed for correctness, regressions and quality, without anything being edited.

verify.name: Verify
verify.instructions: Inspect the requested scope and report actual evidence.

review.name: Review
review.instructions: Inspect the actual requested changes for correctness, regressions, missing tests and maintainability. Return prioritized actionable findings with file/symbol evidence. A completed assessment can contain defects: explicitly state whether the changes are acceptable and what remains unresolved.

route.when: Something is broken or failing and the user wants the cause found: an error message, a failing test, wrong behavior or a regression. A fix plan is wanted, not yet the fix itself.

debug.name: Debug
debug.instructions: Reproduce the reported failure with the smallest relevant check, distinguish observed evidence from hypotheses, identify the root cause and specify a regression test. Report missing prerequisites explicitly; do not edit files or install dependencies.

route.when: The user has a requirement or earlier findings and wants a design or an ordered implementation plan before any code is written: 'how should we build X', 'plan this', 'design the approach'. Often the follow-up after an investigation.
